## Introduction

This data explainer pack is designed to summarise and illustrate four key datasets commonly used to characterise the area and by key decision makers. It is anticipated that the summaries shown here will inform readers how information within the datasets can be visualised and illustrate how similar datasets can be represented.



## Area Summary

Castle ward summary  


## 2021 Census Data

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) conduct a population census every 10 years, providing a snapshot of the UK population, with the next census to be undertaken in 2031. 

Data collected by the census includes:

* Demographics
* Health
* Education
*	Employment and work
*	Housing
* Travel and transport

This data is used by local authorities, the NHS, schools and businesses to allocate funding and plan services. Data from previous censuses are also available to understand social and economic trends. 


```{r,echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}

age_sex_hastings_total<-age_sex_hastings |> group_by(Sex..2.categories.,Age..6.categories.) |> 
  summarise(total=sum(Observation))

ggplot(age_sex_hastings_total)+
  geom_linerange(aes(x = Age..6.categories., ymin = 0, ymax = total, colour = Sex..2.categories.), 
                 position = position_dodge(width = 1))+

             position = position_dodge(width = 1))+
  coord_flip()+xlab("Age")+ylab("Total Count")+labs(color='Sex') 

```

## Community Life Survey

```{r,echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}

Hastings_CLS_reduced |> group_by(LocAtt) |> count() |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=LocAtt,y=n))+geom_bar(stat="identity",fill="lightgreen",colour = "darkgreen")+
  ylab("Frequency")+xlab("Response")+labs(title = "When people get involved in their local area they can change the way the area is",
       subtitle = "1 - Definitely agree, 5 - Definitely disagree")


```


```{r,echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
## Network plot to see the relationships

# Remove total and none column
groups <- Hastings_CLS_unpaidhelp[,1:13]

# Create co-occurrence matrix
co_mat <- t(as.matrix(groups)) %*% as.matrix(groups)

# Remove self-connections
diag(co_mat) <- 0

# Convert to edge list
edges <- as.data.frame(as.table(co_mat)) |>
  rename(from = Var1,
         to = Var2,
         weight = Freq) |>
  filter(weight > 0)

# Remove duplicate edges
edges <- edges |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(pair = paste(sort(c(from, to)), collapse = "_")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct(pair, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-pair)

# Node frequencies
nodes <- data.frame(
  name = colnames(groups),
  freq = colSums(groups)
)

# Create graph
g <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = edges,
  vertices = nodes,
  directed = FALSE
)



edges <- edges |>
  filter(weight >= 3)

labels <- c(
  FUnPd1A = "Raising money",
  FUnPd1B = "Committee member",
  FUnPd1C = "Encouraging others",
  FUnPd1D = "Helping to run",
  FUnPd1E = "Visiting people",
  FUnPd1F = "Mentoring",
  FUnPd1G = "Giving advice",
  FUnPd1H = "Admin",
  FUnPd1I = "Transport",
  FUnPd1J = "Representing",
  FUnPd1K = "Campaigning",
  FUnPd1L = "Other practical help",
  FUnPd1M = "Other help"
)

nodes<-cbind(labels,nodes)

nodes<-nodes |> select(labels,freq)

# Plot
ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight),
                 alpha = 0.5,
                 colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = freq),
                  colour = "orange") +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = labels),
                 repel = TRUE) +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.5, 5)) +
  theme_void()

```

## Crime Data

The police make datasets on street-level crime, outcomes and stop and searches from December 2013. The data includes information on:

*	the force that provided the data about the crime,
*	geolocation of the crime,
* crime type,
*	last outcome,
*	reason for stop and search,
*	demographic data.

Crime data can be used to highlight issues within the local area, in particular around safety, and, as with the census data, aid in supporting funding applications.

